title: Git & Version Control
description: Track changes, collaborate with teams, and manage code history with Git and GitHub.

topics.title: Initializing Repositories
topics.content: git init creates a new repository in the current directory. git clone <url> copies an existing remote repository. The .git folder stores all version history. Never commit sensitive files — use .gitignore to exclude them.

topics.title: Staging & Committing
topics.content: git add stages changes for the next commit. git add . stages everything, git add -p stages interactively. git commit -m 'message' creates a snapshot. Write imperative commit messages: 'Add login form' not 'Added login form'.
topics.command:
git add .
git commit -m "Add user authentication"

topics.title: Branching & Merging
topics.content: git branch <name> creates a branch, git checkout -b <name> creates and switches. Merge integrates another branch's changes. Rebase replays commits on top of another branch for a linear history.
topics.command:
git checkout -b feature/login
git merge main
git rebase main

topics.title: Remote Operations
topics.content: git remote add origin <url> links a local repo to a remote. git push sends commits, git pull fetches and merges. git fetch downloads without merging — safer when you want to review first.
topics.command:
git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git
git push -u origin main
git pull origin main

title: Command Line Essentials
description: Navigate filesystems, manage processes, and automate tasks from the terminal.

topics.title: Navigation
topics.content: pwd prints the current directory. ls lists files, ls -la shows hidden files with details. cd changes directory — cd .. goes up, cd ~ goes home. Tab completion speeds up typing.

topics.title: File Operations
topics.content: mkdir creates directories, touch creates empty files. cp copies, mv moves or renames. rm deletes files, rm -r deletes directories. Use rm carefully — there is no undo.
topics.command:
mkdir -p src/components
touch index.html
cp config.json config.backup.json

topics.title: Searching & Filtering
topics.content: grep searches file contents, find locates files by name. pipe (|) chains commands. head and tail show the beginning or end of files. wc counts lines, words, and characters.
topics.command:
grep -r "TODO" src/
find . -name "*.js" -type f
cat log.txt | grep ERROR | wc -l

title: Database Fundamentals
description: Understand relational databases, SQL queries, and schema design patterns.

topics.title: CRUD Operations
topics.content: INSERT adds rows, SELECT reads, UPDATE modifies, DELETE removes. Always use WHERE clauses with UPDATE and DELETE to avoid affecting all rows. LIMIT constrains result count.

topics.title: Joins & Relationships
topics.content: INNER JOIN returns matching rows from both tables. LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table plus matches. Foreign keys enforce referential integrity. Junction tables handle many-to-many relationships.
topics.command:
SELECT u.name, o.total
FROM users u
INNER JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id
WHERE o.status = 'completed';

topics.title: Schema Design
topics.content: Normalize to reduce redundancy: 1NF eliminates repeating groups, 2NF removes partial dependencies, 3NF eliminates transitive dependencies. Index columns used in WHERE and JOIN clauses. Add constraints like UNIQUE and NOT NULL to enforce data quality.

title: API Design & REST
description: Design clean RESTful APIs with proper HTTP methods, status codes, and resource naming.

topics.title: REST Principles
topics.content: REST APIs use HTTP methods on resource URLs. GET reads, POST creates, PUT replaces, PATCH partially updates, DELETE removes. Use plural nouns for collections: /users not /user. Nest for relationships: /users/1/posts.
topics.command:
GET    /api/users        # List users
POST   /api/users        # Create user
GET    /api/users/1      # Get user 1
PATCH  /api/users/1      # Update user 1
DELETE /api/users/1      # Delete user 1

topics.title: Status Codes & Errors
topics.content: 200 OK for success, 201 Created for POST success, 204 No Content for DELETE success. 400 Bad Request for validation errors, 401 Unauthorized for missing auth, 403 Forbidden for insufficient permissions, 404 Not Found. 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected failures.
topics.command:
200 OK           — Success
201 Created       — Resource created
400 Bad Request   — Validation failed
401 Unauthorized  — Not authenticated
404 Not Found     — Resource missing
429 Too Many Requests — Rate limited
